# eventpipe
`eventpipe` ingests events from two independent channels and is expected to expose one normalized
event to its consumers.
| Channel | Package | Transport | Native record |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file_events` | `plugins/file_events/` | JSON Lines document | `FileEventRecord` |
| `message_events` | `plugins/message_events/` | JSON document of messages | `MessageRecord` |
Both plugins are **vendored**: their modules, public functions, error codes, defaults and native
field names are a compatibility surface. Consumers already depend on `parse_document`,
`parse_line`, `coerce_level`, `split_tags`, `parse_timestamp`, `coerce_priority`,
`normalize_labels` and `stringify_payload` exactly as they behave today.
`core/` is the shared layer:
| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `core/contracts.py` | The unified event model every consumer sees: `NormalizedEvent`, `Severity`, `Plugin` |
| `core/errors.py` | The shared error vocabulary (`AdapterError` and subclasses) |
| `core/adapter.py` | Turns one channel-native mapping into a `NormalizedEvent` |
| `core/registry.py` | Registers the plugins and dispatches a payload to the right one |
The two channels do not share field names, timestamp units or severity vocabularies: every rule a
channel uses is defined inside that channel's own package, and the unified model lives in `core`.
`core/` is the only package that is expected to change; the plugin packages and `core/contracts.py`
describe behaviour that other code already relies on.
## Layout
```text
core/
  contracts.py   errors.py   adapter.py   registry.py
plugins/
  file_events/      schema.py  parser.py  converters.py  errors.py
  message_events/   schema.py  parser.py  converters.py  errors.py
samples/
  events.jsonl   messages.json
tests/
  test_file_plugin.py        native behaviour of the file channel
  test_message_plugin.py     native behaviour of the message channel
  test_public_contract.py    the unified contract
```
## Running the suite
```sh
python3 -B -m pytest -q tests
```

unfinished.

=== core/contracts.py
"""The unified event contract.
Everything downstream of normalization sees only :class:`NormalizedEvent`. Its rules are part of the
project's public surface, so they are stated here once and nowhere else:
``event_id``
    The event's identifier, globally unique across channels. A channel whose native identifier is
    already a string keeps it; a channel whose native identifier is a number is prefixed with the
    channel's short name, e.g. message ``1041`` becomes ``msg-1041``.
``source``
    The registered channel name (``file_events``, ``message_events``).
``kind``
    The event type in lowercase, dot-separated or underscored as the channel wrote it
    (``build.started``, ``user_join``).
``occurred_at``
    A timezone-aware timestamp, stored in UTC. A naive timestamp is never accepted: it cannot be
    ordered against the other channel's events.
``severity``
    Exactly one of :class:`Severity`. Channels translate their own vocabulary into these four words.
``attributes``
    Flat ``str -> str`` data. Values are always strings; a channel that carries numbers or booleans
    renders them through its own converter before they reach this model.
``tags``
    A tuple of non-empty lowercase strings, sorted and free of duplicates.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from enum import StrEnum
from typing import Any
from .errors import NormalizationError

class Severity(StrEnum):
    """The only severity words the unified model knows."""
    DEBUG = "debug"
    INFO = "info"
    WARNING = "warning"
    ERROR = "error"

SEVERITY_VOCABULARY: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(item.value for item in Severity)

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class NormalizedEvent:
    """One event, in the shape every consumer of ``eventpipe`` reads."""
    event_id: str
    source: str
    kind: str
    occurred_at: datetime
    severity: Severity
    attributes: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    tags: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not isinstance(self.event_id, str) or not self.event_id.strip():
            raise NormalizationError("event_id must be a non-empty string")
        if not isinstance(self.kind, str) or not self.kind.strip():
            raise NormalizationError(f"{self.source}: kind must be a non-empty string")
        occurred = self.occurred_at
        if not isinstance(occurred, datetime):
            raise NormalizationError(f"{self.source}: occurred_at must be a datetime")
        if occurred.tzinfo is None or occurred.utcoffset() is None:
            raise NormalizationError(
                f"{self.source}: occurred_at must be timezone-aware",
                code="naive_timestamp",
            )
        object.__setattr__(self, "occurred_at", occurred.astimezone(UTC))
        try:
            severity = Severity(self.severity)
        except ValueError:
            raise NormalizationError(
                f"{self.source}: severity {self.severity!r} is not one of "
                f"{list(SEVERITY_VOCABULARY)}",
                code="unknown_severity",
            ) from None
        object.__setattr__(self, "severity", severity)
        attributes = self.attributes or {}
        if not isinstance(attributes, Mapping):
            raise NormalizationError(f"{self.source}: attributes must be a mapping")
        for key, value in attributes.items():
            if not isinstance(key, str) or not isinstance(value, str):
                raise NormalizationError(
                    f"{self.source}: attributes must map strings to strings; "
                    f"got {key!r}: {type(value).__name__}",
                    code="non_string_attribute",
                )
        object.__setattr__(self, "attributes", dict(sorted(attributes.items())))
        tags = tuple(self.tags or ())
        for tag in tags:
            if not isinstance(tag, str) or not tag.strip():
                raise NormalizationError(f"{self.source}: tags must be non-empty strings")
        object.__setattr__(self, "tags", tags)
    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """JSON-ready projection, used by the CLI and by the evidence exporters."""
        return {
            "event_id": self.event_id,
            "source": self.source,
            "kind": self.kind,
            "occurred_at": self.occurred_at.isoformat(),
            "severity": self.severity.value,
            "attributes": dict(self.attributes),
            "tags": list(self.tags),
        }

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Plugin:
    """One registered channel: its name and the function that decodes a payload into native records.
    ``parse`` returns the channel's records already rendered as plain mappings (each plugin record
    exposes ``as_mapping``). It never normalizes: interpretation belongs to the shared layer.
    """
    source: str
    description: str
    parse: Callable[[Any], tuple[Mapping[str, Any], ...]]

__all__ = [
    "SEVERITY_VOCABULARY",
    "NormalizedEvent",
    "Plugin",
    "Severity",
]
=== core/adapter.py
"""Channel-independent normalization.
This is the only module in the project that knows more than one channel exists. Each channel keeps
its own vocabulary in its own package; the job here is to translate a channel-native record into the
unified model from :mod:`core.contracts` without inventing rules the channel does not already
define.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping
from typing import Any
from .contracts import NormalizedEvent
from .errors import NormalizationError, UnknownSourceError
#: A channel-native mapping -> unified event.
Normalizer = Callable[[Mapping[str, Any]], NormalizedEvent]
_NORMALIZERS: dict[str, Normalizer] = {}

def register_normalizer(source: str, normalizer: Normalizer) -> None:
    """Bind a channel name to its normalizer. Re-registration replaces the previous binding."""
    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source.strip():
        raise ValueError("a normalizer must be registered under a non-empty channel name")
    if not callable(normalizer):
        raise ValueError(f"the normalizer for {source!r} is not callable")
    _NORMALIZERS[source] = normalizer

def supported_sources() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Registered channel names, sorted."""
    return tuple(sorted(_NORMALIZERS))

def normalize_event(source: str, raw: Mapping[str, Any]) -> NormalizedEvent:
    """Turn one channel-native record into a :class:`NormalizedEvent`.
    The record is a mapping as the plugin produced it (``Plugin.parse``); an unknown channel and a
    record that is not a mapping are shared-layer failures and are refused here. Everything else —
    defaults, aliases, timestamp units, attribute rendering — belongs to the channel.
    """
    normalizer = _NORMALIZERS.get(source)
    if normalizer is None:
        raise UnknownSourceError(source, known=supported_sources())
    if not isinstance(raw, Mapping):
        raise NormalizationError(
            f"{source}: a native record must be a mapping, got {type(raw).__name__}",
            code="wrong_record_type",
        )
    return normalizer(raw)

def normalize_file_event(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> NormalizedEvent:
    """``file_events`` native mapping -> unified event.
    Use the file channel's own converter functions; a rule re-derived here will disagree with the
    channel the first time a producer adds a level spelling.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("file_events records are not normalized yet")

def normalize_message_event(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> NormalizedEvent:
    """``message_events`` native mapping -> unified event.
    The message channel's native identifier is numeric and its payload values are not strings; both
    facts are handled by the channel's own converters, not here.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("message_events records are not normalized yet")

def _install_defaults() -> None:
    from plugins.file_events import SOURCE as FILE_SOURCE
    from plugins.message_events import SOURCE as MESSAGE_SOURCE
    register_normalizer(FILE_SOURCE, normalize_file_event)
    register_normalizer(MESSAGE_SOURCE, normalize_message_event)

_install_defaults()

__all__ = [
    "Normalizer",
    "normalize_event",
    "normalize_file_event",
    "normalize_message_event",
    "register_normalizer",
    "supported_sources",
]
=== core/registry.py
"""The plugin registry and the single dispatch entry point.
Registration is explicit and Host-side: nothing is discovered by walking a directory, so a payload
can never introduce a channel. Dispatch is the only place where a payload becomes normalized events,
and it is the only place that decides their order.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Any
from .contracts import NormalizedEvent, Plugin
from .errors import PluginRegistrationError, UnknownSourceError

class PluginRegistry:
    """Channel name -> plugin, plus dispatch."""
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._plugins: dict[str, Plugin] = {}
    # -- registration --------------------------------------------------------
    def register(self, plugin: Plugin) -> None:
        if not isinstance(plugin, Plugin):
            raise PluginRegistrationError(f"register() takes a Plugin, got {type(plugin).__name__}")
        if not plugin.source.strip():
            raise PluginRegistrationError("a plugin must declare a non-empty channel name")
        if not callable(plugin.parse):
            raise PluginRegistrationError(f"channel {plugin.source!r} has no usable parser")
        if plugin.source in self._plugins:
            raise PluginRegistrationError(f"channel {plugin.source!r} is already registered")
        self._plugins[plugin.source] = plugin
    def sources(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """Registered channel names, sorted."""
        return tuple(sorted(self._plugins))
    def plugin(self, source: str) -> Plugin:
        try:
            return self._plugins[source]
        except KeyError:
            raise UnknownSourceError(source, known=self.sources()) from None
    # -- decoding ------------------------------------------------------------
    def parse(self, source: str, payload: Any) -> tuple[Mapping[str, Any], ...]:
        """Decode a payload into channel-native records. No normalization happens here."""
        return self.plugin(source).parse(payload)
    def dispatch(self, source: str, payload: Any) -> tuple[NormalizedEvent, ...]:
        """Decode and normalize one payload.
        The returned sequence is ordered by ``(occurred_at, event_id)`` across every event of the
        payload, so two consumers reading the same payload see the same order even when the channel
        itself emits another one.
        """
        # The channel is known and its records decode; only the normalization step is missing.
        self.parse(source, payload)
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "PluginRegistry.dispatch does not normalize yet: it must return unified events in "
            "event order"
        )

def build_default_registry() -> PluginRegistry:
    """The registry every entry point builds: both vendored channels, nothing else."""
    from plugins.file_events import SOURCE as FILE_SOURCE
    from plugins.file_events import parse_document as parse_file_document
    from plugins.message_events import SOURCE as MESSAGE_SOURCE
    from plugins.message_events import parse_document as parse_message_document
    registry = PluginRegistry()
    registry.register(
        Plugin(
            source=FILE_SOURCE,
            description="JSON Lines document of build and deployment events",
            parse=lambda payload: tuple(
                record.as_mapping() for record in parse_file_document(payload)
            ),
        )
    )
    registry.register(
        Plugin(
            source=MESSAGE_SOURCE,
            description="chat backend message log",
            parse=lambda payload: tuple(
                record.as_mapping() for record in parse_message_document(payload)
            ),
        )
    )
    return registry

__all__ = ["PluginRegistry", "build_default_registry"]
=== core/errors.py
"""The shared error vocabulary of the normalization layer.
Channel plugins raise their own errors; the shared layer never rewrites them into its own type,
because a caller that branches on ``FileEventError.code`` must keep seeing that code. These classes
exist for the failures that belong to the shared layer itself: an unregistered channel, a record the
unified model cannot represent, a plugin that cannot be registered.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Any

class AdapterError(Exception):
    """A failure of the shared layer, carrying a stable machine-readable code."""
    code = "adapter_error"
    def __init__(self, message: str, *, code: str | None = None, detail: Any = None) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message
        if code is not None:
            self.code = code
        self.detail = detail
    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.code}: {self.message}"

class UnknownSourceError(AdapterError):
    """No plugin is registered under the requested channel name."""
    code = "unknown_source"
    def __init__(self, source: str, *, known: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            f"no plugin is registered for channel {source!r}; known channels: {list(known)}",
            code="unknown_source",
            detail={"source": source, "known": list(known)},
        )
        self.source = source
        self.known = known

class NormalizationError(AdapterError):
    """A channel-native record that the unified model refuses to represent."""
    def __init__(self, message: str, *, code: str = "normalization_failed", detail: Any = None):
        super().__init__(message, code=code, detail=detail)

class PluginRegistrationError(AdapterError):
    """A plugin cannot be registered: duplicate channel name, or no usable parser."""
    code = "plugin_registration_failed"

__all__ = [
    "AdapterError",
    "NormalizationError",
    "PluginRegistrationError",
    "UnknownSourceError",
]

1	"""The unified event contract.
2	
3	Everything downstream of normalization sees only :class:`NormalizedEvent`. Its rules are part of the
4	project's public surface, so they are stated here once and nowhere else:
5	
6	``event_id``
7	    The event's identifier, globally unique across channels. A channel whose native identifier is
8	    already a string keeps it; a channel whose native identifier is a number is prefixed with the
9	    channel's short name, e.g. message ``1041`` becomes ``msg-1041``.
10	``source``
11	    The registered channel name (``file_events``, ``message_events``).
12	``kind``
13	    The event type in lowercase, dot-separated or underscored as the channel wrote it
14	    (``build.started``, ``user_join``).
15	``occurred_at``
16	    A timezone-aware timestamp, stored in UTC. A naive timestamp is never accepted: it cannot be
17	    ordered against the other channel's events.
18	``severity``
19	    Exactly one of :class:`Severity`. Channels translate their own vocabulary into these four words.
20	``attributes``
21	    Flat ``str -> str`` data. Values are always strings; a channel that carries numbers or booleans
22	    renders them through its own converter before they reach this model.
23	``tags``
24	    A tuple of non-empty lowercase strings, sorted and free of duplicates.
25	"""
26	
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping
30	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
31	from datetime import UTC, datetime
32	from enum import StrEnum
33	from typing import Any
34	
35	from .errors import NormalizationError
36	
37	
38	class Severity(StrEnum):
39	    """The only severity words the unified model knows."""
40	
41	    DEBUG = "debug"
42	    INFO = "info"
43	    WARNING = "warning"
44	    ERROR = "error"
45	
46	
47	SEVERITY_VOCABULARY: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(item.value for item in Severity)
48	
49	
50	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
51	class NormalizedEvent:
52	    """One event, in the shape every consumer of ``eventpipe`` reads."""
53	
54	    event_id: str
55	    source: str
56	    kind: str
57	    occurred_at: datetime
58	    severity: Severity
59	    attributes: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
60	    tags: tuple[str, ...] = ()
61	
62	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
63	        if not isinstance(self.event_id, str) or not self.event_id.strip():
64	            raise NormalizationError("event_id must be a non-empty string")
65	        if not isinstance(self.kind, str) or not self.kind.strip():
66	            raise NormalizationError(f"{self.source}: kind must be a non-empty string")
67	
68	        occurred = self.occurred_at
69	        if not isinstance(occurred, datetime):
70	            raise NormalizationError(f"{self.source}: occurred_at must be a datetime")
71	        if occurred.tzinfo is None or occurred.utcoffset() is None:
72	            raise NormalizationError(
73	                f"{self.source}: occurred_at must be timezone-aware",
74	                code="naive_timestamp",
75	            )
76	        object.__setattr__(self, "occurred_at", occurred.astimezone(UTC))
77	
78	        try:
79	            severity = Severity(self.severity)
80	        except ValueError:
81	            raise NormalizationError(
82	                f"{self.source}: severity {self.severity!r} is not one of "
83	                f"{list(SEVERITY_VOCABULARY)}",
84	                code="unknown_severity",
85	            ) from None
86	        object.__setattr__(self, "severity", severity)
87	
88	        attributes = self.attributes or {}
89	        if not isinstance(attributes, Mapping):
90	            raise NormalizationError(f"{self.source}: attributes must be a mapping")
91	        for key, value in attributes.items():
92	            if not isinstance(key, str) or not isinstance(value, str):
93	                raise NormalizationError(
94	                    f"{self.source}: attributes must map strings to strings; "
95	                    f"got {key!r}: {type(value).__name__}",
96	                    code="non_string_attribute",
97	                )
98	        object.__setattr__(self, "attributes", dict(sorted(attributes.items())))
99	
100	        tags = tuple(self.tags or ())
101	        for tag in tags:
102	            if not isinstance(tag, str) or not tag.strip():
103	                raise NormalizationError(f"{self.source}: tags must be non-empty strings")
104	        object.__setattr__(self, "tags", tags)
105	
106	    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
107	        """JSON-ready projection, used by the CLI and by the evidence exporters."""
108	
109	        return {
110	            "event_id": self.event_id,
111	            "source": self.source,
112	            "kind": self.kind,
113	            "occurred_at": self.occurred_at.isoformat(),
114	            "severity": self.severity.value,
115	            "attributes": dict(self.attributes),
116	            "tags": list(self.tags),
117	        }
118

120	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
121	class Plugin:
122	    """One registered channel: its name and the function that decodes a payload into native records.
123	
124	    ``parse`` returns the channel's records already rendered as plain mappings (each plugin record
125	    exposes ``as_mapping``). It never normalizes: interpretation belongs to the shared layer.
126	    """
127	
128	    source: str
129	    description: str
130	    parse: Callable[[Any], tuple[Mapping[str, Any], ...]]

132	
133	__all__ = [
134	    "SEVERITY_VOCABULARY",
135	    "NormalizedEvent",
136	    "Plugin",

138	]

3	This is the only module in the project that knows more than one channel exists. Each channel keeps
4	its own vocabulary in its own package; the job here is to translate a channel-native record into the
5	unified model from :mod:`core.contracts` without inventing rules the channel does not already

12	from typing import Any
13	
14	from .contracts import NormalizedEvent
15	from .errors import NormalizationError, UnknownSourceError

17	#: A channel-native mapping -> unified event.

22	
23	def register_normalizer(source: str, normalizer: Normalizer) -> None:
24	    """Bind a channel name to its normalizer. Re-registration replaces the previous binding."""
25	
26	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source.strip():

2	
3	Channel plugins raise their own errors; the shared layer never rewrites them into its own type,
4	because a caller that branches on ``FileEventError.code`` must keep seeing that code. These classes
5	exist for the failures that belong to the shared layer itself: an unregistered channel, a record the
6	unified model cannot represent, a plugin that cannot be registered.

1	"""The plugin registry and the single dispatch entry point.
2	
3	Registration is explicit and Host-side: nothing is discovered by walking a directory, so a payload
4	can never introduce a channel. Dispatch is the only place where a payload becomes normalized events,
5	and it is the only place that decides their order.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	from collections.abc import Mapping
11	from typing import Any
12	
13	from .contracts import NormalizedEvent, Plugin
14	from .errors import PluginRegistrationError, UnknownSourceError
15	
16	
17	class PluginRegistry:
18	    """Channel name -> plugin, plus dispatch."""
19	
20	    def __init__(self) -> None:
21	        self._plugins: dict[str, Plugin] = {}
22	
23	    # -- registration --------------------------------------------------------
24	
25	    def register(self, plugin: Plugin) -> None:
26	        if not isinstance(plugin, Plugin):
27	            raise PluginRegistrationError(f"register() takes a Plugin, got {type(plugin).__name__}")
28	        if not plugin.source.strip():
29	            raise PluginRegistrationError("a plugin must declare a non-empty channel name")
30	        if not callable(plugin.parse):
31	            raise PluginRegistrationError(f"channel {plugin.source!r} has no usable parser")
32	        if plugin.source in self._plugins:
33	            raise PluginRegistrationError(f"channel {plugin.source!r} is already registered")
34	        self._plugins[plugin.source] = plugin
35	
36	    def sources(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
37	        """Registered channel names, sorted."""
38	
39	        return tuple(sorted(self._plugins))
40	
41	    def plugin(self, source: str) -> Plugin:
42	        try:
43	            return self._plugins[source]
44	        except KeyError:
45	            raise UnknownSourceError(source, known=self.sources()) from None
46	
47	    # -- decoding ------------------------------------------------------------
48	
49	    def parse(self, source: str, payload: Any) -> tuple[Mapping[str, Any], ...]:
50	        """Decode a payload into channel-native records. No normalization happens here."""
51	
52	        return self.plugin(source).parse(payload)
53	
54	    def dispatch(self, source: str, payload: Any) -> tuple[NormalizedEvent, ...]:
55	        """Decode and normalize one payload.
56	
57	        The returned sequence is ordered by ``(occurred_at, event_id)`` across every event of the
58	        payload, so two consumers reading the same payload see the same order even when the channel
59	        itself emits another one.
60	        """
61	
62	        # The channel is known and its records decode; only the normalization step is missing.
63	        self.parse(source, payload)
64	        raise NotImplementedError(
65	            "PluginRegistry.dispatch does not normalize yet: it must return unified events in "
66	            "event order"
67	        )

81	            source=FILE_SOURCE,

83	            parse=lambda payload: tuple(
84	                record.as_mapping() for record in parse_file_document(payload)

17	DEFAULT_PRIORITY = 3

19	#: Priority -> this channel's canonical severity name.

21	    1: "debug",
22	    2: "info",
23	    3: "info",
24	    4: "warning",

30	    """Return a priority in ``1..5``, defaulting to ``DEFAULT_PRIORITY`` when it is absent.
31

33	    is treated.

38	    if not isinstance(raw_priority, int) or isinstance(raw_priority, bool):
39	        raise MessageEventError("wrong_type", "priority must be an integer")
40	    if not PRIORITY_TO_SEVERITY.get(raw_priority):
41	        raise MessageEventError(
42	            "priority_out_of_range",
43	            f"priority {raw_priority} is outside {sorted(PRIORITY_TO_SEVERITY)}",

55	def parse_timestamp(value: Any) -> datetime:
56	    """Convert epoch milliseconds into an aware UTC datetime."""
57	
58	    if not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool):
59	        raise MessageEventError("wrong_type", f"sent_at must be integer milliseconds: {value!r}")
60	    try:
61	        return datetime.fromtimestamp(value / 1000.0, tz=UTC)
62	    except (OverflowError, OSError, ValueError) as error:

67	    """Return the labels as a sorted, lowercased, duplicate-free tuple of non-empty strings."""

72	    return tuple(sorted(label for label in seen if label))

87	    if isinstance(value, int):
